newBeyondSource: Runtime configuration surface for the recorder: the source's five switches (log directory, file logging, debug output, console output, 10000-char buffer threshold) were private fields requiring a recompile to change, while its own docs told users to 'set them in config' (QUIRK-14, business rule 24). DIAG CAPTURE exposes all five plus level filter, timestamp mode and redaction.

DIAG STATUS: an in-band health signal. The source's acceptance criterion 20 records that a completely dead logging subsystem was indistinguishable from a healthy one on every channel, because all four internal-failure reports went to a debug-trace sink compiled out of every non-DEBUG build (QUIRK-11). STATUS reports armed state, sink health, buffer occupancy, fault count and last fault.

DIAG TAIL: a read surface for the buffer and the rolling files, with level/regex/since filtering, buffer+file merge, per-entry chunking, and transparent .gz reading. The source's GetLogs() was public API with no user-facing surface anywhere.

DIAG RECORD as a pipeline tee: records each chunk as an entry and re-emits it verbatim (or swallows it with -quiet), with OnStartPipe/OnEndPipe journal brackets, making every other package's pipeline observable in one log.

DIAG ROTATE: retention by age, total-size cap, per-file size roll and optional gzip, dry-run by default and confined to the log root. The source had no retention policy at all -- 'rotation' meant only a date-stamped file name, with no size cap, no compression and no deletion, so long-lived installs grew unboundedly.

DIAG DOCTOR: an executable form of the source's 300-line 0xC0000005 troubleshooting document. Groups runtime, build, backend, native, credentials, config, storage. Includes an OUT-OF-PROCESS native load probe so a hard access violation cannot kill the shell.

DIAG DOCTOR credential checks that report resolution tier and source label only, never a value -- explicitly refusing to reproduce the source's migration wizard, which interpolated plaintext secrets into 'set CHATDBG_...=<value>' lines on every settings load (credential Q3).

DIAG DOCTOR build-profile checks (BLD-001..004) that warn when trimming, AOT, invariant globalization, resource-key exception messages or stripped stack-trace metadata are degrading the very diagnostics this package produces (packaging Q12/Q13/R21/R24/R38).
DIAG DOCTOR real keystore probe that distinguishes 'available' from 'present but refusing', replacing the source's bare 'is the OS Windows' test which reported a policy-disabled vault as healthy.

DIAG AUDIT: structured command-execution auditing with redaction policy, plus an honest printed caveat that the framework's AuditMaskingConfiguration only masks '-name=value' tokens and not its own space-separated '-name value' form.

DIAG BUILDINFO: identity and publish-profile of the running artefact plus the loaded tool-package inventory. The source declared its version in three unreconciled places and its Compact profile stripped assembly identity entirely.

DIAG FILES -roots: names the product's three per-user state roots and their writability. The source scattered state across three roots under two naming conventions and documented none of them outside Windows.

Ingest-time credential redaction in the recorder ([REDACTED] placeholder matching the framework default), so pasted or wizard-printed secrets never reach a file users are told to attach to bug reports.

Repair of QUIRK-4/QUIRK-18: export sources the union of un-flushed buffer and already-flushed daily files, writes no file when there is nothing to write, refuses to overwrite a non-empty destination without -force, and reports success/failure to the caller.
Bounded buffer with counted drop markers when the file sink is off, replacing the source's unbounded growth (business rule 13).
Invariant-culture timestamp rendering by default, fixing the source's build-dependent double timestamp shape (QUIRK-13), with an opt-in localoffset/utc mode.
Refusal of the empty-app-data-root case that silently turned the source's log directory into a working-directory-relative path on a Unix host with no HOME.
openDesignQuestions: Daily file-name pattern: the chapter renames the default from 'llamasharp_yyyyMMdd.log' to 'chatdbg_yyyyMMdd.log' because the rebuilt recorder captures all three backends, and keeps read-compatibility with the legacy name. If the support workflow's documented artefact name is treated as a contract, this must be reverted.

Whether DIAG RECORD's suffix message parameter should be blocked entirely for interactive use, given that the framework's audit masking cannot mask space-separated parameters. The chapter mitigates by recording only length+hash in audit metadata, but a stricter reading argues for a prompt-based input path instead.

Whether the recorder should own or merely borrow the process-global native log-sink hook when the binding offers no unregister. The chapter specifies swapping to a no-op sentinel on disposal; the underlying binding's actual capability was not verified.

Whether DIAG DOCTOR's read-only ports into settings and credential provenance should be host-supplied interfaces or a formal cross-package query contract. The chapter chose host-supplied ports to keep the tool -> SDK dependency arrow, at the cost of check groups reporting 'skipped (no provider)' in a bare host.

Whether the DIAG tools that need shared configuration should use global environment variables (requiring modifiesEnvironment: true on CAPTURE/ROTATE/AUDIT) or a host-injected policy object. The chapter chose globals to stay inside the framework's documented propagation rules; a policy object would be simpler but less inspectable via ENV.
Whether -probe native's out-of-process helper is acceptable in a restricted host, or whether it should be a separate opt-in package so the base DIAG package never spawns a process.

Retention defaults (14 days, 256 MiB total, 64 MiB per file) are invented -- the source had no retention at all and the dossier records 'could not determine whether the daily file was ever intended to be pruned'. These need a product decision.

Whether DIAG DOCTOR should also fail (not warn) when maxTokens is inert on the Azure non-logprobs path and when llamaGpuDevice/llamaThreads/llamaBatchSize reach no runtime, or whether those source quirks should be fixed in the owning packages instead of merely reported here.

newBeyondSource: PROMPT RENAME — rename preserving description, createdAt and lastUsedAt (source could only export/import/delete, which reset all metadata)
PROMPT COPY — duplicate a prompt under a new name (source always started new prompts from the same generic default text)
PROMPT RESET — explicit, idempotent restoration of the four built-ins, including a single named built-in (source seeded only when the store loaded zero prompts, at every launch)
PROMPT PATH — report store/exchange/backup directories, how resolved and whether writable (source's list output printed a .NET type name instead of the directory, dossier Q2)
PROMPT DOCTOR — diagnose unreadable files, name/file-name mismatches, sanitization collisions, dangling active name, missing built-ins; -fix applies only reversible repairs
Lossless JSON import/export format carrying description, createdAt and lastUsedAt (source exported text only, losing all metadata on a round trip)
Content authoring through the pipe and through -file, plus -text and -editor, on both CREATE and EDIT (source's create never accepted content; edit was a raw-console END loop only)
Editing a prompt's description from the command surface (source allowed this only in the GUI dialog)
Filtering, sorting, result-shaping and a clamped -limit on LIST (-name-like, -text-like, -sort, -collation, -format, -unused, -builtin)
-content-only on STATUS and SHOW, making prompt text a first-class pipeline source
-force / -yes confirmation model on every overwriting or destructive tool, with confirmation defaulting to No (source's GUI focused Yes and had no active-prompt delete guard)
Single-generation .backup copies before EDIT, DELETE and RESET -force, plus a .quarantine area for unreadable files
Path confinement: no tool accepts a filesystem path; import/export resolve bare file names against one configured exchange directory (source read and wrote any path the process could reach)
Platform-pinned behaviour: one fixed forbidden-character set, ordinal case-sensitive name matching, selectable collation, and an export directory that never degrades to the working directory
Atomic temp-file-plus-rename writes with an advisory lock, closing the source's concurrent-clobber and truncation window
Content size ceiling (CHATDBG_PROMPT_MAX_CHARS) and end-of-input termination in the interactive editor, closing the source's unbounded-memory hang
Store relocation via CHATDBG_PROMPT_DIR (source had a constructor override used only by its tests)
Distinguishing a corrupt prompt record from a missing one in SHOW (source reported both as 'not found')
openDesignQuestions: Registration mode for PROMPT USE: it needs modifiesEnvironment: true to publish CHATDBG_SYSTEM_PROMPT globally, but package-directory loading registers every discovered command with modifiesEnvironment: false. Is the package always registered in-process by the composition root (Cupcake path (a)), or must the store marker file <store>/.active become the primary selection channel with the environment as a mirror?

Ownership of persistence for the active prompt name: this chapter has USE publish to the environment and ChatDbg.Tools.Settings persist systemPromptName. That requires Settings to observe an environment change or to be invoked as a later pipeline stage (PROMPT USE | SET SAVE). Confirm with the Settings chapter which mechanism is contractual.

Does the host's IIoContext implementation propagate an output encoder and branch on ResultFormat? The framework never applies IOutputEncoder itself, so PROMPT LIST -format csv/json is metadata only unless the shell's HandleOutputChunk renders on it.

The argument tokenizer strips ':' '/' '\' ';' '<' '>' '{' '}' '+' '=' ',' even inside quotes. This chapter routes all paths and all real content around it (basenames, pipe, -file, interactive prompt). If the host is permitted to fork or wrap NamesValidator to preserve quoted spans verbatim, several parameters (-text, -description, real paths) could be restored — is that fork acceptable?

Backup policy: one generation in <store>/.backup is specified. Should PROMPT DOCTOR be able to restore from it (a RESTORE verb), or is that deliberately left to the exchange directory plus real version control?

Should the exchange directory default to the documents folder (source's command-path default) or to a dedicated ChatDbg subdirectory? The chapter keeps the documents folder for continuity, but a dedicated directory would make confinement easier to explain and to lock down.

Culture-sensitive collation is the default to match the source exactly, but the source's size-optimised publish profiles disabled globalization and silently changed it. Should the shipped release pin -collation ordinal by default and keep culture as opt-in?

PROMPT EDIT -editor spawns a process, the only such capability in the package. Confirm whether the restricted-host profile disables it by default (CHATDBG_PROMPT_ALLOW_EDITOR=false) rather than enabling it by default as specified here.

openDesignQuestions: Environment prefix for sub-commands: the framework prefixes seeded environment values with '{COMMANDNAME}_', but it is not settled in ref-command.md whether that name is the root token (SET) or the sub-command (SHOW). The spec assumes the root and reads defensively (SET_FILE, then bare FILE) until the host pins it with a test.
Whether -format yaml ships in v1: it costs a YamlDotNet 16.3.0 dependency in a package that otherwise has none. JSON and CSV are sufficient for every composition in the chapter.
Profile inheritance (a 'base' field so profile B inherits A and overrides three keys) is deliberately out of v1: it turns validation into a graph problem and SET DIFF into a three-way merge.

Whether the framework's widened boolean grammar (1/0/yes/no/on/off) should be adopted for boolean keys, as specified, or narrowed back to the source's strict true/false. The spec adopts the framework grammar deliberately.
Whether a corrupt settings document should block writes until an explicit SET RESET/SET IMPORT (as specified) or be silently overwritten on the next successful write (source behaviour).
Whether the host should run 'SET SHOW -format json | SET VALIDATE -strict' at startup in place of the source's ad-hoc configuration self-check, and what it should do with a non-clean result.
newBeyondSource: Named configuration profiles as a first-class concept: list, show, switch, save, drop, and diff (SET PROFILE, SET PROFILES, SET SAVEPROFILE, SET DROPPROFILE, SET DIFF). The source explicitly provided 'no profiles, no per-workspace settings, no config-file layering, no --config override'.
Single-value read (SET GET) — the source's only read surface was a 46-line dump.

Clearing a setting (SET UNSET). The source's arity rule rejected a bare '/set azureEndpoint' and there was no reset/unset/clear verb anywhere, so no text setting could be returned to empty from the command surface.
Restore-to-defaults (SET RESET), with -backup. The source had no reset path at all; the only way back to defaults was deleting the file out of band.

A generated, machine-readable key catalog (SET KEYS) replacing three hand-maintained, mutually inconsistent lists in the source (the ~72-line /set help, the dump's static Setup Commands block, and the 'Unknown setting' error that named 13 of ~26 keys).

Configuration validation as a tool (SET VALIDATE), including provider-name case checking, GGUF existence, prompt-name resolution, cross-platform keystore-toggle checking and plaintext-secret detection. The source validated only at the moment of a /set write; hand-edited documents were read verbatim.
Whole-document import with merge, dry-run and backup (SET IMPORT).
Machine-readable output formats (-format json|yaml|csv) on the read tools, making configuration pipeable into other packages and into a chat turn.

Publishing the effective configuration into the controller environment as CHATDBG_* keys instead of sharing a mutable settings object between commands — the fix for the source's worst bug (Q4/Q26), where the windowed shell's commands mutated and persisted a stale defaults record the UI never read.

azureApiVersion promoted to a real setting (default 2023-12-01-preview). The source hard-coded it in the request URL while /logprobs debug advised users to change an API version they had no way to change (Q33).

Explicit, always-reported clamping (-clamp / SET_STRICT) unifying the source's two contradictory out-of-range policies — text commands rejected, the windowed dialog clamped silently and ignored unparseable input entirely.

Invariant-culture parsing and formatting in every build configuration (the source used ambient culture and forced invariant only in Compact/SingleFile builds, so the same command was accepted by one binary and rejected by another).
Atomic temp-file-plus-rename document writes and a save failure that surfaces as a command failure (the source printed to stdout and still reported success — invisible in the windowed shell).
Validation parity between SET MODEL and SET VALUE modelId (the source's /model bypassed every rule /set modelId enforced on the same field).

Dry-run on every mutating tool, and confirmation-by-flag (-force plus SET_CONFIRM) instead of the source's blocking stdin prompts inside a service, which were invisible and unanswerable under the full-screen shell.
SET ENV, preserving the Xcaciv.Command built-in SET semantics after this package claims SET as a root command.
Cross-platform credential-store toggle (useOsCredentialStore, wire name unchanged) that cannot be enabled where no store exists — closing the windowed dialog's missing platform gate.

openDesignQuestions: Chunk granularity for VIEW TOKENS output: one chunk per rendered line, per grid row, or one chunk for the whole rendering? Per-line streams best through the bounded channel but means a downstream stage sees a table in pieces; the chapter specifies per-line (list) and per-row (grid), which should be confirmed against the host's terminal sink.

VIEW SAMPLE, VIEW TOKENS (grid) and VIEW HEAT (sampling) must buffer, which defeats the framework's lazy streaming for long responses. Is the 100000-chunk default ceiling right, and should the host lower it via PipelineConfiguration.MaxChannelQueueSize instead?

The framework prefixes per-command environment keys with the COMMAND name, not the root, so a sub-command named LAYOUT or STATUS would collide across packages. The chapter routes around this with fully-qualified CHATDBG_VIEW_* globals and modifiesEnvironment:true registrations — confirm the host is willing to grant that permission to four tools.

Invoking the bare root 'VIEW' throws InvalidOperationException from CommandFactory and the async path is less forgiving than the sync one on an unknown sub-command. The host must catch and render usage; no tool can absorb it. Confirm where that mapping lives.

Should the default palette really change from the source's bands5 to bands10? The chapter argues yes (bands5 fed unit-scale values rendered every real token red), but it is a visible behavioural change and needs an explicit sign-off.

Should the plain-table alternatives cap of 2 and the styled-table cap of 3 be preserved as per-surface compatibility defaults rather than unified on the setting? The chapter unifies; a -compat flag was considered and dropped.
Should the left-justified rule stay 79 characters while the centred rule is 80? Preserved as the source's asymmetry, but it looks like a defect to anyone reading the output.
Precision default is 5 (matching both table renderers) while the shared value formatter used 2. Which should a fresh installation see?
Who owns enabling virtual-terminal processing on legacy Windows consoles — the chapter assigns it to the host at start-up and has VIEW CAPS only observe the result. Confirm.

Does the full-screen host consume VIEW TOKENS output as text into its probability panel, or does it need a structured intermediate shape? The panel's 50-column default, max(longest+5,50) sizing and 0-based numbering are host constants that the renderer's 1-based output must be reconciled with.
Should VIEW TRANSCRIPT offer any redaction hook? It renders message content verbatim, including anything a user pasted, and a host that logs its output is logging conversation content.

openDesignQuestions: Argument tokenization strips ':' '/' '\\' and '=' even inside quoted spans (NamesValidator.InvalidParameterChars), so no filesystem path, endpoint URL, or Bedrock model id such as 'anthropic.claude-3-sonnet-20240229-v1:0' can survive the command line. The chapter routes around it with catalog handles, piped values, and a -revision parameter — but if the framework ever relaxes the filter, MODEL SELECT and MODEL LOAD should take raw values directly and the workaround should be retired.

GetDefaultEnvironment() values are seeded under the SUB-COMMAND name prefix (LOAD_, TEST_, CATALOG_), not the root, so private-bucket keys can collide with an identically-named sub-command in another package. Confirm whether the host should namespace buckets, or whether this package should abandon the private bucket entirely and keep its breadcrumbs in the process singleton.

Should the local satellite assembly be run out of process by default? An access violation inside the native engine is uncatchable and kills the shell with the user's unsaved conversation; a supervised subprocess isolates it but loses raw logits, prompt-token logits and custom sampling stages.

The source clamped the request-side top-K to 1-20 AND used the same setting as the local sampler's top-K, so local generation was always top-5 limited out of the box even with introspection off. Decide whether MODEL TUNE should expose a separate sampler top-K, or whether the coupling stays (and is merely disclosed by MODEL CAPS).

Fabricated log-probabilities are removed. Confirm with the product owner that the demo affordance the fabrication served is fully covered by an explicit demo command elsewhere, since MODEL CAPS will now report 'logprobs: no' for Bedrock where the source silently showed a populated visualisation.

Bedrock family detection is widened from the source's bare 'anthropic.' prefix to '^(?:[a-z]{2}\\.)?anthropic\\.' so cross-region inference profiles match. Confirm no other geography prefix shape is in use before pinning that regex.
The generation and model-load locks are process-wide, unbounded and un-cancellable in the source. This chapter specifies a bounded wait plus a status message; the timeout value is not yet chosen.
Catalog TTLs (15 min cloud, 60 s local) and the handle-stability guarantee are asserted, not derived from any source behaviour; they need a product decision.

MODEL CAPS -probe on a cloud backend can cost a billable completion. Confirm whether the default should stay 'declared only' or whether a host-level policy should forbid -probe entirely in shared/CI contexts.
newBeyondSource: MODEL CATALOG — model/deployment/weight-file discovery with token-safe short handles; the source had zero model-id validation on any path and shipped a default ('gpt-4') that is not a valid Bedrock identifier.

MODEL CAPS — an honest per-backend capability and ceiling report (logprobs, top-K max, prompt-side logprobs, streaming, tool calling, temperature/token/context ceilings, cancellation), with an explicit declared-vs-verified distinction.
MODEL TEST — a six-stage connectivity/credential/entitlement probe; the source performed no URL parsing, no scheme check, no key-shape check and no connectivity probe anywhere.

MODEL STATUS — reports what is actually resident plus a drift table naming every configured value that differs from the loaded one; the source silently ignored hardware and system-prompt changes until the model path changed or the process restarted.
-timeout on MODEL TEST (clamped 1-300s) — the source configured no timeout anywhere; the only bound was the transport's ~100s default.
-force on MODEL LOAD and -apply on MODEL TUNE — the escape hatch for the source's path-change-only reload rule.
Threads, batch size and GPU device are actually applied to inference; the source validated, persisted and displayed all three and never passed them to the engine.
-no-mmap and -mlock flags — the source hard-wired memory-mapping on and memory-locking off with no override.
-revision on MODEL SELECT — reassembles a ':'-delimited model version suffix that the framework's argument tokenizer strips.
Cancellation of an in-flight turn is reported as a capability; the source threaded no cancellation token anywhere in the product.

AWS_SESSION_TOKEN support is declared and reported by MODEL TEST; the source read no session token, so temporary/STS credentials in the environment were silently downgraded to a key pair and failed authentication.
Azure API version is a settings key (defaulting to the source's hard-coded 2023-12-01-preview) rather than an uneditable literal.
GGUF magic-number check as a warning at MODEL SELECT and a stage in MODEL TEST; the source treated any existing file, including a zero-byte one, as a configured model.
Bedrock family detection widened to match cross-region inference profiles (us.anthropic.*) that the source's bare 'anthropic.' prefix test routed down the wrong payload path.
Fabricated ('simulated') log-probabilities are removed outright; MODEL CAPS plus a capability-gated TOKEN LOGPROBS ENABLE replace them.
Upstream error bodies are truncated to 200 characters and credential-masked before display; the source echoed entire upstream error pages into the terminal.

OS keystore unavailability is reported explicitly ('unavailable on this platform') instead of degrading silently, and MODEL LOAD degrades to CPU with a named warning when no GPU backend exists for the RID.
Package split into a restricted-host-safe primary assembly and a native-dependent satellite, merged under one MODEL root.

openDesignQuestions: Environment prefix confirmation: sub-commands are dispatched through their root, so the key CommandController passes to GetChild(commandName) should be CHAT, not SEND — meaning all twelve tools share one environment bucket keyed CHAT_. The chapter states this and flags it for verification at integration; if the framework actually keys per sub-command, every GetDefaultEnvironment declaration and every prefixed read in the package changes.

How IConversationBackend reaches a tool when the package is crawled from the plugin directory rather than registered in-process. CommandFactory only consults an IServiceProvider when Type.GetType resolves the type, which it will not for an isolated AssemblyContext load. The chapter's answer is that SEND/RETRY degrade with a stated failure in that case, but a host that wants a crawled package to talk to a backend needs a mechanism the framework does not currently offer.

Whether CHAT EXPORT should keep the source's silent overwrite as the default (chosen) or flip to -noclobber-by-default. The chapter preserves silent overwrite and removes the actual harm via atomic temp-and-rename, but this is the one preserved quirk most likely to be challenged.
Whether restoring the imported createdAt (a deliberate correction of source quirk Q7) can break byte-for-byte round-trip expectations for anyone diffing exported files against source-produced ones.

Confirmation UX inside a pipeline: PromptForCommand is only defined when HasPipedInput is false, so POP -count>1, CLEAR and RETRY refuse rather than prompt. If the host later gains an out-of-band confirmation channel, that refusal should become a prompt.
Whether -validate should default to warn (chosen) or off (exact source behaviour). warn changes observable output for existing files containing non-whitelisted roles.
Session file format and whether a session file is simply an exported conversation document plus a name/lastUsed sidecar, or a distinct schema. The chapter assumes the former but does not pin it.

Audit masking: the framework's shipped AuditMaskingConfiguration.ApplyMasking only rewrites -name=value tokens and is effectively non-functional for space-separated syntax, so CHAT SEND's full prompt text lands in audit events verbatim. The host must supply its own IAuditMaskingConfiguration; the exact contract for that is left to the host chapter.
newBeyondSource: Streaming replies (CHAT SEND -stream on, default) — the source blocked the prompt until the provider answered, with no streaming, spinner, elapsed display or cancellation.
Per-turn transient overrides for provider, model, temperature, max tokens, top-K and system prompt that never touch the persisted settings.
Request timeout (-timeout) — the source had no cancellation token anywhere in the product.
CHAT LIST — the conversation record is emitted as chunks; the plain-console source could not display the record at all, and the pipeline needs a source.
CHAT RETRY — discard the last reply and re-send the preceding user turn with different settings, optionally emitting the discarded reply; replaces a manual pop-and-retype sequence.
Named, listable, switchable, forkable sessions (CHAT SESSIONS / CHAT USE / CHAT NAME) with a persistent session store — the source had no autosave, no autoload, and a session id nothing ever read.
CHAT POP -count and structured JSON output of removed messages, making a pop recoverable by piping it to CHAT EXPORT.
CHAT CLEAR -keep system, -newsession and -backup.
CHAT APPEND -command, which makes the record's dormant isCommand flag reachable (nothing in the source ever set it).
Confirmation prompts on destructive operations (POP -count>1, CLEAR, RETRY, IMPORT replace) — the source had none anywhere, and its GUI put Clear History one keystroke from Pop Last Message.
Atomic export (temp file + rename) replacing the source's in-place whole-file overwrite that could leave a truncated file where a valid history used to be.

Underlying failure reasons delivered in the failure chunk instead of printed to stdout — the source's persistence diagnostics painted over the full-screen shell and left the user a cause-free message.
Import safety: -validate warn|off|strict role checking (the source validated nothing) and -maxbytes with a 32 MiB default (the source read whole files with no cap).
Optional path containment via CHAT_EXPORT_ROOT / CHAT_IMPORT_ROOT plus session-name sanitization and component-wise, symlink-resolved containment — the source had no path restrictions whatsoever.
Additional export formats: jsonl, md and text alongside the byte-compatible json.

Corrections to misleading output: inject reports the index actually used; pop appends '...' only when truncation occurred and cuts on grapheme boundaries; import restores the createdAt it used to discard; role matching for filtering is case-insensitive everywhere.
-norecord on CHAT SEND, to ask a question without polluting the context under test.
A note emitted when the active backend is llama and an edited turn is one the local path ignores (the source's local paths read only the last user message and ignored the isCommand flag silently).

openDesignQuestions: Generalizing the store tier off Windows contradicts a source test that asserts a vault write returns false on every non-Windows host (WindowsCredentialManagerTests.cs:18-26). The spec deliberately generalizes; that test must be rewritten as 'wincred is unavailable off Windows' rather than deleted, and the product owner must sign off on the change.

Ownership of the settings-file tier: CRED emits `SET CLEARCRED <slot>` request chunks rather than editing settings.json. That inter-package request protocol is asserted here but not specified anywhere - the SET package chapter must define the chunk grammar, or the two packages must agree on a shared contract assembly.

The no-echo prompt convention (a prompt string prefixed `secret:` is read with echo suppressed) is a HOST requirement that IIoContext cannot express - PromptForCommand takes only a string. Either the ChatDbg IO context adopts the sentinel convention, or the framework needs a PromptForSecret member.

Whether `encfile` should exist at all. It is the only tier where this package stores a secret itself, and on a platform with no OS keystore it is either a real improvement over plaintext or a false sense of security depending on how the key is derived. The key-derivation policy is unspecified here.

Whether the per-machine salt used for CRED SCAN fingerprints should be shared across machines so that two machines' scans can be compared. Sharing it makes fingerprints correlatable (useful for fleet audits) and slightly more attackable.

The AWS provider's fallback to the SDK's own ambient credential chain is a fourth, undocumented credential channel the rebuild inherits unless it is closed. CRED DOCTOR reports it; nobody has decided whether the provider package should disable it.

Whether CRED ENABLE/DISABLE should be registered with modifiesEnvironment:true so the store flag is a global variable. The spec recommends no (CRED_-prefixed keys reach the private bucket without the grant), but that makes the flag invisible to tools that do not know the bucket convention.

Backup entries created by CRED ROTATE -keepbackup have no expiry and no lifecycle. Nothing prunes them, which reintroduces a milder version of the source's 'stored secrets are never cleaned up' problem.
newBeyondSource: Cross-platform secret stores: macOS Keychain, Linux Secret Service/libsecret, and an encrypted-file fallback, alongside the byte-compatible Windows Credential Manager backend (the source was Windows-only, with a test pinning the refusal).
Secret deletion (CRED REMOVE) - the source shipped a CredDelete primitive with zero call sites in the entire repository, so revocation was impossible inside the product.
Secret rotation with read-back verification, optional backup entry, and a warning when a higher-priority tier still shadows the newly rotated value (CRED ROTATE).

Secrets never travel as command-line parameters - forced by the framework's argument scrubber (which deletes / \ = + : ; from arguments) and by the fact that AuditMaskingConfiguration only masks -name=value tokens. Values arrive from a no-echo prompt or one piped chunk.
A pipeline-native redactor (CRED REDACT) that overrides Main so it scrubs upstream FAILURE chunks' ErrorMessage too, making any other package's output safe by composition.
A plaintext-leak scanner (CRED SCAN) reporting salted 4-character fingerprints instead of values, plus settings-file permission and temp-directory-location findings the source never checked.

Live backend probing (CRED STORES -probe) with distinct reasons, replacing the source's bare 'is the OS Windows' availability test which declared a policy-disabled Windows credential service available.
An environment-channel discovery tool (CRED ENV) naming all five variables, their priority order and their occupancy - the source's README documented none of them.

A credential readiness diagnostic (CRED DOCTOR) that checks BOTH halves of a key pair individually and reports the provider SDK's ambient credential chain as a visible fourth channel, correcting two source defects.
Credential profiles (-profile) namespacing store entries as ChatDbg:<profile>:<Slot>, so one OS user can keep two ChatDbg configurations apart.
Value validation before storage: empty rejection, a stated 1280-UTF-16-character ceiling, and control-character rejection - the source performed no check at all.

Truthful outcome reporting: declining consent is a success rather than 'Failed to enable...'; migration reports per-slot results instead of always returning success; store, save and OS failures surface their real reason instead of being swallowed at two nested layers.
Dry-run planning (CRED MIGRATE -dryrun) and unattended operation (-yes) so credential custody can run in CI without blocking on a prompt nobody can answer.
A four-outcome resolution report that distinguishes 'store error' from 'entry not found' from 'not supported on this platform' - the source collapsed all three into a silent null.
Structured, non-disclosing audit records per operation (slot, tier, backend, profile, outcome). The source had no logging or audit of credential operations of any kind.

newBeyondSource: Derived statistics the source never computed: per-step truncated top-K entropy (nats or bits), normalized entropy, perplexity, mean negative log-likelihood, chosen-vs-runner-up margin, confidence-band counts and low-confidence ratio (TOKEN STATS)
A composable confidence filter with -below/-above/-band/-marginbelow/-range plus the source's sampling rule and an opt-in -dedupe (TOKEN FILTER)
Reading an exported analysis back in (TOKEN LOAD), which the source had no path for at all — this is what makes the whole package testable and runnable with no model, network or backend
Comparing two analyses token by token with text or index alignment (TOKEN DIFF)

Real export: the source's export-analysis was a stub that returned success and wrote no file; EXPORT actually writes json/jsonl/csv/md, prompts before overwrite, and offers -redact to share numbers without content

A stable analysis document schema (analysis/token/attribution/stats/diff records, one JSON object per pipeline chunk) with schemaVersion, analysis ids and a bounded process-scoped ring of the last N analyses, replacing the source's single mutable list cleared at every generation

No-fabrication guarantee: where the source silently substituted synthetic probability data when a provider returned none (and its own tests pinned that behaviour), the rebuild emits zero token records plus a stated reason; only TOKEN DEMO fabricates, and every record it emits is stamped synthetic:true

One probability scale (0-1 internally, percent at the edge) and one indexing rule (0-based document, 1-based display), replacing the source's three incompatible scales, doubled '%%' and mixed 0-/1-based surfaces
Cross-platform determinism for the demonstration data (documented 64-bit xorshift instead of the platform RNG seeded 42) and invariant-culture number formatting throughout
A pipeline-safe consent gate: io.PromptForCommand when interactive, -yes when piped, instead of the source's blocking Console.ReadLine that had no console under a terminal UI
Named attribution methods (recency/attention/gradient) with a real normalized recency weight, replacing the source's hard-coded constant InfluenceScore of 0.8
-context, -temperature, -seed, -nobos, -samplesize, -maxgen, -lowconf, -print, -redact, -force, -dedupe, -invert, -perstep, -stopafter, -as parameters

Pure-managed, trim/AOT-safe package with no native dependency and no reflection, so it is safe to load under AssemblySecurityPolicy.Strict — correcting the source's reflection-based logit accessor that failed silently under its own publish profile and reported 100% confidence in everything
openDesignQuestions: Sibling package names and root commands are assumed, not confirmed: ChatDbg.Tools.Providers (AI), ChatDbg.Tools.Rendering (RENDER), ChatDbg.Tools.Settings (CONFIG), ChatDbg.Tools.History (CHAT), ChatDbg.Tools.Diagnostics (LOG). If the other chapters chose different names or roots, §6.1 and the compositions in §6.4 need to be reconciled.

How does a plugin-loaded command reach host services? Xcaciv.Command's CommandFactory activates ALC-loaded plugin commands via a public parameterless constructor with no DI injection, so I specified a shared ChatDbg.Introspection.Abstractions assembly in the default load context plus a static IntrospectionServices registry. The architect should confirm this is the product-wide pattern rather than a per-package invention.

Environment seeding for sub-commands is unverified: CommandController.Run derives the command name from the first token, so a child environment is built as GetChild("TOKEN") and only the TOKEN bucket is copied, while CommandRegistry.GetEnvironment seeds per-registered-command buckets (and would try to instantiate the synthetic root, whose FullTypeName is empty). Every tool therefore supplies its own in-code fallback defaults; whether the framework actually seeds anything for sub-commands should be tested against 3.3.4.

Command-line file paths are unusable in this framework (the argument tokenizer strips backslash, forward slash, colon, equals inside quotes as well as outside), so EXPORT/LOAD take a filename stem resolved against TOKEN_EXPORTDIR. If the product needs arbitrary destinations, the host must add a path-alias mechanism — this is a product-wide decision, not a package-local one.

Whether the settings-dialog clamp semantics survive: the source rejected out-of-range top-K from commands but silently clamped in the GUI settings dialog (1-20). This chapter rejects everywhere; if the rebuilt GUI reintroduces a dialog, the divergence must be resolved in one direction.

Whether the source's verbatim user-visible strings should be preserved character-for-character where they contain defects, e.g. 'Error: Response text expected, none recieved.' (misspelling) and 'Unknown subcommand: {arg}. ' (trailing space). This chapter preserves the trailing space and drops the misspelling by not carrying that string; the product needs one policy.

Whether the truncated top-K entropy should be reported at all, given it is only a lower bound on the true distribution's entropy. The alternative is to report it only when the backend can supply full-vocabulary logits. Currently it is always reported with entropyIsTruncated:true.

Attribution beyond the recency heuristic: -method attention and -method gradient are declared and refuse when unavailable, but no backend contract for attention export or gradient attribution is specified here. Whoever owns ChatDbg.Tools.Providers must decide whether IAttributionModel is real or the two methods should be dropped from the allow-list.

Whether TOKEN INSPECT should exist at all given SPLIT + MAP + ATTRIBUTE compose to the same thing. It is kept for source parity and for the single-model-load optimisation, but it is the one tool in the catalog that is pure convenience.

Analysis retention: TOKEN_KEEP defaults to 8 in-memory analyses. Whether analyses should instead be written through to TOKEN_EXPORTDIR automatically (making the ring a cache rather than the store) is undecided and affects TOKEN DIFF's ergonomics.

openDesignQuestions: Who owns the operator identity recorded in a trust grant? The host knows only an OS user name; a shared machine or a service account makes 'who granted this' ambiguous, and the chapter assumes the host can supply something better than the process account.

Should PKG RELOAD attempt a real collectible-ALC unload at all? The chapter deliberately never claims one (unload is terminal, returns four indistinguishable falses, and CommandExecutor does not dispose command instances). If the host later holds every plugin reference behind a single draining wrapper, a genuine hot-swap becomes possible and PKG RELOAD's contract would change.

Package signature verification on Linux has no platform code-signature analogue; the design drops the policy from require to prefer with a warning. Is a detached-signature scheme over the package manifest (operator-supplied trusted keys) worth specifying, or does that duplicate what the feed's own package signing already provides?

-deps allow acquires a transitive closure, but Xcaciv.Loader does not confine dependency loads to basePathRestriction. Should PKG instead flatten and rewrite deps.json at install time, or refuse any package whose deps.json probes outside its own directory?

Whether PKG should be able to install into the system package root at all under an explicit elevated-install mode, or whether that must remain entirely out-of-band deployment tooling as specified here.

The lockfile records feed names, but a name is machine-local. A shared lockfile referencing feed 'corp' restores only if the receiving machine has a feed by that name; embedding the URL instead would make the lockfile a redirection vector. The chapter chose names - this trade-off is worth a second opinion.
newBeyondSource: A runtime extension mechanism of any kind: the source product had none - 18 command classes were new-ed by hand into a Dictionary<string, ICommand> in each shell, and three were never registered at all.

Package acquisition that actually completes: download, artefact-identity re-read, safe extraction, digest recording and placement into the crawler's {id}/{version}/bin layout (Cupcake downloads and then leaves extraction and dependency resolution as TODOs).
An explicit four-state trust model (quarantined / blocked / sandboxed / trusted) with an interactive, unforceable, non-pipeable grant that requires typing back the package id and a SHA-256 prefix.
Publisher-identity verification (package signature, plus platform code-signature where one exists), which Xcaciv.Loader never performs - it verifies bytes, not provenance.
An allowlist-first integrity posture: digests recorded at install, re-checkable on demand (PKG VERIFY), with learning mode never enabled in production.
Inventory and introspection - what is installed, what is loaded, what each package registers and what rights it asked for - none of which exists anywhere in the source or in Cupcake.
Update and rollback with a semver bound, side-by-side installation, retained previous versions, and a mandatory trust reset on every version change.
Uninstall that also purges digest and trust records, with deferred deletion when assemblies are locked and an honest statement that unload is not guaranteed.

Feed management: named sources, mandatory package-source mapping, mandatory HTTPS, a per-request timeout (Cupcake's wrapper passes CancellationToken.None everywhere), and credential-slot indirection so a feed token is never stored by this package.
A diagnostic tool (PKG DOCTOR) whose whole purpose is converting the loading stack's three layers of silent skipping into named findings, without loading any package code.
A portable lockfile keyed by relative paths and content digests, which regenerates the loader's non-portable absolute-path hash store on the target machine at restore time.
Hot re-scan (PKG RELOAD) that closes Cupcake's parked search -> install -> reload loop, and reports precisely which half of it the runtime cannot deliver.

Audit records for every supply-chain act (PackageVerified, PackageRejected, TrustGrant, TrustRevoked, PackageBlocked, HashMismatch, PolicyWeakened, PackagesReloaded), with digests reported only as prefixes and expected/actual pairs kept out of the user-readable trail.
